brief: great_candy ground pickup: the same wrapped-sweet form in a blue and silver wrapper with a subtle sparkle; more premium than good_candy
author: Claude (coordinator-side Meshy item-prop worker), owner-authorized Meshy use (Standing owner direction 1, 15 Oct 2026)
workflow: agent-drafted multi-view concept from repo references (Meshy image-to-image nano-banana-pro, references as data URIs) -> inspected -> Meshy 3D (latest, quad remesh, PBR textures embedded in GLB)
target_size_m: about 0.25 m along the longest horizontal axis (game scales pickups up for readability)

native_size.note: Meshy raw GLB, longest side ~1.9 units

scale_normalisation.method: lossless: GLB scene roots wrapped in node 'metres_root' with uniform scale + translation; base at y=0, footprint centred on x/z

previews: preview_3view.png (software flat-shaded 3-view, colours sampled per face)
files.raw_glb: not published (identical mesh to glb_metres minus the metres_root node)

concepts.prompt: Game pickup item concept: ONE single wrapped hard sweet candy lying on its side, the classic bow-tie candy-wrapper silhouette: a plump rounded oval sweet in the middle with the wrapper twisted tight at both ends and fanning out into two crinkled flared wrapper tails. Premium wrapper: rich sky-to-royal blue body with polished metallic silver bands and silver foil twisted tails, a small embossed silver star on the front, glossy foil sheen with a few subtle tiny white sparkle glints. The underside is slightly flattened so it rests flat on the ground. Same family and finish as the wrapped gold candies in the first reference (chunky soft-bevelled forms, hand-painted PBR look) but only one sweet: no cloth, no pile. Stylised Palworld-like game prop, chunky readable silhouette that reads clearly from far away, about 0.25 m long. Single isolated object, centred, three-quarter elevated view, plain neutral grey background, even studio lighting, no text, no logos, no characters, no ground. Strictly no red, pink, maroon or oxblood anywhere.
references: tb/meshy-props assets/props/meshy-1020/candy_pickup_set/model_candy_rare/preview_3view.png (middle 3/4 panel cropped (360,0)-(720,360), upscaled 2x; local derived file rare_34.png): the published rare_candy pickup, judged 6.90, used as family style reference

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MJohnsonWellabe/Tetherbound/main/docs/reference/tetherbound-meadows-keyart.png (downscaled to 1024 px; local derived file keyart_small.png): Meadows palette and finish
concepts.verdict: rejected: correct colours and an embossed silver star, but every view stood the sweet upright (or tilted on a diagonal) and the body was a taller egg shape than good_candy, so it would not share the form or lie flat

concepts.prompt: Game pickup item concept: ONE single wrapped hard sweet candy lying HORIZONTALLY on its side, exactly the same shape, proportions and bow-tie silhouette as the green candy in the first reference (plump rounded oval sweet in the middle, wrapper twisted tight at both ends, two crinkled flared wrapper tails pointing left and right), shown as the premium tier of the same candy family. Premium wrapper: rich sky-to-royal blue body with two polished metallic silver bands, silver foil twisted tails, a small embossed silver star on the front, glossy foil sheen with a few subtle tiny white sparkle glints. The underside is slightly flattened so it rests flat on the ground. Chunky soft-bevelled forms and hand-painted PBR finish like the wrapped candies in the second reference, but only one sweet: no cloth, no pile. Stylised Palworld-like game prop, chunky readable silhouette that reads clearly from far away, about 0.25 m long. Single isolated object, centred, seen from a three-quarter elevated angle with the candy lying flat, plain neutral grey background, even studio lighting, no text, no logos, no characters, no ground. Strictly no red, pink, maroon or oxblood anywhere.

concepts.verdict: CHOSEN (views 0 front with star and 1 end as multi-image input; view 2 is the starless back): generated with the good_candy concept as shape reference, so it is the same lying bow-tie sweet; sky-to-royal blue body, two silver bands, embossed silver star, silver foil tails, a few white sparkle glints

visual_verdict: Good: the same lying bow-tie wrapped sweet as good_candy (built from the good concept as shape reference), in sky-to-royal blue with two metallic silver bands, polished silver foil tails and an embossed silver star on the front, with a few white sparkle glints painted into the texture. It reads clearly as the premium tier beside good_candy and matches the blue star great_candy UI icon. Final extents 0.25 x 0.10 x 0.10 m, base at y=0; contact as for good_candy (rounded body plus tail tips). The sparkle is texture-only and small; at 10-15 m it will need the pickup's existing glint/emissive presentation to show. Metallic silver depends on scene reflections and may look grey under flat Compatibility lighting. Single material (PBR, textures embedded), 13,939 triangles (about 7k quads).
integration_note: candidate only; stays flag-off until its scene passes code-blind judging
palette_check: no red/oxblood/pink requested or observed (base-colour texture scan: 0 red/pink pixels); sky and royal blue body, metallic silver bands, star and tails, white glints
